# Kubernetes Manifests for AI Gov Review Service

This directory contains Kubernetes manifests for deploying the AI Gov Review Service to EKS with CloudNativePG PostgreSQL.
page_texts.2:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#files]

## Files

- `namespace.yaml` - Namespace for the service
- `postgres-cluster.yaml` - CloudNativePG cluster (3 replicas with HA)
- `postgres-pooler.yaml` - PgBouncer connection pooler
- `configmap.yaml` - Application configuration
- `secret.yaml` - Sensitive configuration (template - populate before deploying)
- `job-migrate.yaml` - **Database migration job (run before deployment)**
- `job-seed-data.yaml` - **Initial template seeding job (one-time setup)**
- `deployment.yaml` - Application deployment with Redis sidecar and migration init container
- `service.yaml` - Kubernetes service
- `ingress.yaml` - Updates shared cluster ingress to add AI Gov Review API paths
- `hpa.yaml` - Horizontal Pod Autoscaler

**Note:** The ingress is shared across services (MkDocs, RAG, AI Gov Review). Each service adds its paths to the same ingress resource. The certificate is managed at the cluster level.
page_texts.3:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#prerequisites]

## Prerequisites

1. **EKS Cluster** - Running with appropriate node groups
2. **CloudNativePG Operator** - Installed in cluster:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg/release-1.22/releases/cnpg-1.22.0.yaml
   ```

3. **AWS Load Balancer Controller** - For ingress
4. **EBS CSI Driver** - For PostgreSQL storage
page_texts.7:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#3-create-secrets]

### 3. Create Secrets

Edit `secret.yaml` to add your actual secrets, then apply:

```bash
kubectl apply -f secret.yaml
```
page_texts.8:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#4-deploy-postgresql-cluster]

### 4. Deploy PostgreSQL Cluster

```bash
kubectl apply -f postgres-cluster.yaml
kubectl apply -f postgres-pooler.yaml
```

Wait for cluster to be ready:

```bash
kubectl wait --for=condition=ready cluster/ai-gov-db -n ai-gov-review --timeout=300s
```
page_texts.9:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#5-run-database-migrations]

### 5. Run Database Migrations

**Option A: Standalone Migration Job (Recommended for initial setup)**

```bash
kubectl apply -f job-migrate.yaml

# Monitor migration progress
kubectl logs -n ai-gov-review job/ai-gov-review-migrate -f

# Wait for completion
kubectl wait --for=condition=complete job/ai-gov-review-migrate -n ai-gov-review --timeout=120s

# Cleanup job after success
kubectl delete job ai-gov-review-migrate -n ai-gov-review
```

**Option B: Init Container (Automatic on deployment)**

The `deployment.yaml` includes an init container that runs migrations automatically before each pod starts. This is useful for rolling updates with schema changes.
page_texts.10:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#6-seed-initial-templates-one-time-setup]

### 6. Seed Initial Templates (One-time setup)

```bash
kubectl apply -f job-seed-data.yaml

# Monitor seeding progress
kubectl logs -n ai-gov-review job/ai-gov-review-seed-templates -f

# Wait for completion
kubectl wait --for=condition=complete job/ai-gov-review-seed-templates -n ai-gov-review --timeout=60s

# Verify templates were created
kubectl exec -it deployment/ai-gov-review-service -n ai-gov-review -c ai-gov-review -- \
  poetry run python -c "
    import asyncio
    from src.db.template_repository import get_template_repository
    async def check():
        repo = get_template_repository()
        templates = await repo.list_active()
        print(f'✅ Found {len(templates)} templates:')
        for t in templates:
            print(f'  - {t.name} (v{t.version})')
    asyncio.run(check())
  "

# Cleanup job after success
kubectl delete job ai-gov-review-seed-templates -n ai-gov-review
```
page_texts.11:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#7-deploy-application]

### 7. Deploy Application

```bash
kubectl apply -f configmap.yaml
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f service.yaml
kubectl apply -f hpa.yaml
```

**Note:** The deployment includes an init container that automatically runs migrations before starting the app. For initial deployments, running the standalone migration job (step 5) is recommended to catch any issues early.

### From local machine (port-forward)

```bash
kubectl port-forward -n ai-gov-review svc/ai-gov-db-rw 5432:5432
psql postgresql://app:yourpassword@localhost:5432/aigovreview
```
page_texts.16:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#backup-and-recovery]

## Backup and Recovery

CloudNativePG automatically backs up to S3. To restore from backup:

```yaml
apiVersion: postgresql.cnpg.io/v1
kind: Cluster
metadata:
  name: ai-gov-db-restored
spec:
  bootstrap:
    recovery:
      source: ai-gov-db
      recoveryTarget:
        targetTime: "2024-01-01 12:00:00"
```

[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#monitoring]

## Monitoring

View cluster status:

```bash
kubectl get cluster -n ai-gov-review
kubectl get pods -n ai-gov-review
kubectl logs -n ai-gov-review ai-gov-db-1
```
page_texts.18:
[.tooling/components/apis/ai-gov-review-service/k8s/README.md#scaling]

## Scaling

Scale application pods:

```bash
kubectl scale deployment ai-gov-review-service -n ai-gov-review --replicas=5
```

PostgreSQL replicas are controlled in `postgres-cluster.yaml` (`instances: 3`).
